get.description: Always ``ok``. Touches no dependency.

Per-dependency readiness.

503 only when a dependency in :data:`REQUIRED_CHECKS` is down; 200 otherwise,
however degraded the optional ones are. Read the per-item statuses for the
detail — the status code is a routing decision, not a summary.

get.summary: The public record behind one tag
get.description:
Recompute, compare, and report. Reads only -- no scan is recorded here.

A GET that wrote a scan row would mean every link preview, every crawler
and every browser prefetch counted as somebody holding the object.

post.summary: Record a scan of one tag
post.description:
Record the scan, score the pattern, attempt the claim, return the record.

Order matters. The scan is written first so the pattern being scored
includes the scan being made -- otherwise the response is always one scan
behind the thing it exists to notice. The claim is attempted after, because
a claim is a consequence of a scan having happened.
Create an account. Does not log the caller in.
Exchange credentials for an access token and a refresh cookie.
Rotate the refresh token and mint a fresh access token.

Revoke the presented token's whole family and clear the cookie.

Idempotent: an absent or unknown token still returns 204. Logout reporting
an error is unhelpful -- the caller wanted to be logged out, and after this
they are.
Revoke every family for the authenticated user.

get.description: The authenticated user's own profile.

patch.description: Update display name and region. No other field is reachable.

get.description:
Which providers are usable right now.

Always 200, even when nothing is configured -- the frontend asks this in
order to decide whether to render a button, and an error would be a worse
answer than ``enabled: false``.
Begin the authorization-code flow. 302 to Google, or 503 if unconfigured.

Handle Google's redirect back.

An identity that already maps to an account gets a full session here. One
that does not gets a pending token and **no session at all** -- no access
token in the redirect, no refresh cookie set. See :mod:`app.auth.pending`.

post.description: Finish a new-identity sign-up: supply a role, get an account and a session.

get.description: Latest version of every category. Public.
Latest active version of one category.
Every published version, oldest first.

One pinned version, retired or not.

Retired versions still resolve: existing items reference them, and a
verification that 404s because a category was retired would be a broken
provenance record.

post.description:
Dry-run an attribute payload against a category. Writes nothing.

Lets a client check a form before submitting it, and gives the live-demo
sequence a real request that proves a just-created category is usable.
Item registration itself is Phase 6.

Rate limited, unlike the reads beside it. This is the only unauthenticated
endpoint in the system that does real work on a caller-supplied body: it
loads a schema and runs a validator over arbitrary JSON. The reads answer
from a cached registry and cost a lookup; this costs compilation, and on a
single free-tier instance an unmetered one of those is a way to spend the
process's CPU from outside with no account and no cost to the caller.

Create a category at v1, usable immediately.

Accepts a category JSON document as the request body, so publishing one on
stage is ``curl -d @banarasi.json`` and nothing else.

Publish v(n+1), and report what it changes.

The diff is returned so the operator sees the consequence at the moment
they cause it, rather than discovering it when registrations start failing.
Existing items are unaffected either way -- they are pinned to their own
version.

patch.description:
Update display name and active flag. Slug and schema are unreachable.

Neither field exists on ``UpdateCategoryRequest``, so no request shape can
change them -- a slug is referenced by URLs and printed tags, and a schema
change is a new version by definition.

post.description: Register an item. Item, event, and outbox row commit together or not at all.

get.description: Keyset page over items, newest first.

post.description: Cut an item into children, enforcing mass balance under a row lock.

get.description: One item with its lineage, children, and current chain state.
Full subtree, depth-annotated. One recursive CTE.

schema.title: Response Read Tree Api V1 Items  Item Id  Tree Get

get.description: Append-only event log, oldest first.

post.summary: Record an attestation about an item
post.description:
Vouch for an item. One attestation per actor per item, enforced by the database.

A second attempt is a 409 from ``uq_attestations_item_attestor``, not from
an application check: a check-then-write has a gap, and two simultaneous
requests would both pass it.

get.summary: List the attestations recorded against an item
get.description: Newest first. Carries roles and pseudonymous references, never identities.

get.summary: Who vouched for this item, and how independent were they
get.description:
Derived on every read from the attestation and dispute sets.

Nothing is cached and nothing is stored, so a fraud flag applied a second
ago is already reflected here.

post.summary: Flag an actor and dispute everything they registered
post.description:
One transaction: the flag, the audit event, and every affected item.

Items the actor *registered* become disputed. Items they merely attested to
are not touched -- their trust level drops on the next read, because the
level is derived and a flagged attestor stops counting.

post.summary: Lift a fraud flag and the disputes it caused
post.description:
Reverses exactly what the flag did, and nothing else.

An item independently disputed by an inspector stays disputed: that finding
is not this flag's to lift.

Stream, bound, sniff, hash, budget, mirror, store, then try to pin.

Returns 201 even when pinning fails or is switched off. The SHA-256 is the
integrity proof and it is already committed; the CID only records where a
copy happens to live, and a pinning service having a bad day is not a reason
to reject a weaver's photograph.

get.description: Every tier this file can be read from right now, best first.

get.summary: Serve the bytes from the best available tier
get.description:
Serve the file, falling through tiers rather than trusting any one.

``tier`` is a preference, not an instruction: the mirror may have been wiped
by a redeploy since the row was written, so a request for it still falls
back to the blob rather than 404ing on a tier that used to exist.

post.description: Only the item's registrant, or an admin.

schema.title: Response List Item Media Api V1 Items  Item Id  Media Get

delete.description:
Removes the link. The media row and its bytes are kept.

The SHA-256 may already be anchored on chain, and deleting the bytes behind
an anchored hash produces exactly the dead reference the three-tier storage
design exists to prevent. "No longer depicts this item" is not "never
existed".

post.summary: Issue a tag code for an item
post.description:
Generate a code, bind it to the item, and record a ``TAG_ISSUED`` event.

409 when the item is already tagged, with the existing code in the error
details: that is a fact to read, not a failure to retry.

get.summary: Render an item's tag as a QR image
get.description:
PNG by default, SVG on request. Error correction Q, four-module quiet zone.

``size`` is a pixel edge for the PNG and the default ``width``/``height`` on
the SVG, which also carries a ``viewBox`` so it scales to any label.

post.summary: Issue tags for many items at once
post.description:
Tag a batch, reporting each item separately.

An already-tagged item or one whose anchoring failed is reported and
stepped over. Rejecting the whole batch for one bad row would make an
operator find and remove it by hand before any of the good ones printed.

get.summary: Queue depth, dead letters, indexer lag, quotas, workers, chain mode
get.description: One read of everything an operator needs before presenting.

BulkTagResult.description: What happened to one item in the batch.

CategoryView.description: The GI category, as a reader would name it.

ChainState.title: ChainState
ChainState.description:
What the chain currently knows. Honest about PENDING.

An item is PENDING until Phase 7's worker sees the required confirmations.
Reporting CONFIRMED before that would be a lie the demo tells, and the whole
proposition is that this record can be trusted.

ChainStatusView.title: ChainStatusView
ChainStatusView.description: What the anchoring path can actually do right now.

ChainView.title: ChainView
ChainView.description: What the chain says, when it was asked, and whether the answer is fresh.

CompleteRequest.title: CompleteRequest
CompleteRequest.description:
Finish a new-identity sign-up.

``role`` is mandatory and is always re-validated against
``SELF_ASSIGNABLE_ROLES`` in the handler. The pending token deliberately
carries no role, so this is the only place one enters the system and the
only place it can be checked. Email is absent: it comes from the verified
provider identity, never from the client.

statement.title: Statement
statement.description: Free-form claim: inspection notes, ledger references, dates.

CreateAttestationRequest.title: CreateAttestationRequest
CreateAttestationRequest.description: A claim one party makes about one item.

CreateCategoryRequest.title: CreateCategoryRequest
CreateCategoryRequest.description:
Create a category at v1.

``schema_version`` is absent on purpose: v1 is implied, and letting a caller
pick a starting version would allow gaps that make "the previous version"
ambiguous.

CreateVersionRequest.title: CreateVersionRequest
CreateVersionRequest.description: Publish v(n+1) of an existing category. Only the schema changes.

DisputeStatus.title: DisputeStatus
DisputeStatus.description: Whether an item's provenance is contested.

FlagActorRequest.title: FlagActorRequest
FlagActorRequest.description: Admin action. The reason is required and is shown on every item it touches.

FlagActorResponse.title: FlagActorResponse
FlagActorResponse.description: What a flag or a clear actually changed, reported back plainly.

InclusionProofView.title: InclusionProofView
InclusionProofView.description:
A batched item's proof that its hash is under the anchored root.

Published because it is checkable without this service: a reader with the
root, the leaf and these siblings can run the same computation offline and
does not have to take the answer on trust.

IndexerStatusView.title: IndexerStatusView
IndexerStatusView.description:
How far behind the event mirror is.

``lag_blocks`` is ``None`` -- not zero -- when the head could not be read.
Zero means caught up, and reporting an unreachable node as caught up is the
single most misleading thing this endpoint could do.

ItemDetail.title: ItemDetail
ItemDetail.description: One item with everything an authenticated caller may see.

ItemListResponse.title: ItemListResponse
ItemListResponse.description: Collection envelope with a keyset cursor, per app.core.pagination.

ItemMediaResponse.title: ItemMediaResponse
ItemMediaResponse.description: One media file as it appears on an item.

ItemStatus.title: ItemStatus
ItemStatus.description: Anchoring state of an item's hash. PENDING until the chain confirms.

MediaDetail.title: MediaDetail
MediaDetail.description: A media row plus every way to read it.

MediaKind.title: MediaKind
MediaKind.description: What a piece of media depicts, per item.

MediaSummary.title: MediaSummary
MediaSummary.description: A media row, without its bytes.

MediaView.title: MediaView
MediaView.description:
One piece of media, addressed by content.

``gateway_url`` is null until the file is pinned. The digest is published
either way: it is the integrity claim, and it is true whether or not
anybody is currently hosting the bytes.

OutboxDepthView.title: OutboxDepthView
OutboxDepthView.description: How many jobs of one type sit in one state.

PinStatus.title: PinStatus
PinStatus.description: IPFS pinning state for a media blob.

ProviderStatusResponse.title: ProviderStatusResponse
ProviderStatusResponse.description: One provider and whether it is usable right now.

PublicEventView.title: PublicEventView
PublicEventView.description:
One provenance event, reduced to its type and its timing.

Payloads are not published. They carry preimages and hashes that belong in
an audit, not on a shop floor, and an event log that publishes its payloads
is a slow leak waiting for somebody to add a field to one.

PublicItemView.title: PublicItemView
PublicItemView.description: Everything a scan of one tag returns.

RefreshRequest.title: RefreshRequest
RefreshRequest.description: Body fallback for clients without a cookie jar.

RegisterItemRequest.title: RegisterItemRequest
RegisterItemRequest.description: Register a new item, or a root of a new provenance tree.

RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest
RegisterRequest.description: New account. ``role`` must be self-assignable; absent means CONSUMER.

ScanBlock.title: ScanBlock
ScanBlock.description: How often this tag has been scanned, and what that pattern looks like.

ScanRequest.title: ScanRequest
ScanRequest.description:
The optional body of a scan.

Both fields are hints. The fingerprint is an opaque string the client
chooses and this service only ever stores hashed; the region is consulted
only when the edge that terminated the connection said nothing.

SchemaDiff.title: SchemaDiff
SchemaDiff.description:
What publishing this version changes, relative to the previous one.

Returned from the create-version endpoint so an operator sees the
consequence at the moment they cause it, rather than discovering it when a
weaver's next registration starts failing.

SplitChild.title: SplitChild
SplitChild.description: One piece cut from a parent.

SplitRequest.title: SplitRequest
SplitRequest.description: Cut a parent into children. Mass balance is enforced across all of them.

SplitResponse.title: SplitResponse
SplitResponse.description: The outcome of a split, with the parent's updated accounting.

StoryView.title: StoryView
StoryView.description: The maker's side of the record, as far as they have allowed.

SystemStatusResponse.title: SystemStatusResponse
SystemStatusResponse.description: The one screen worth checking before presenting.

TagResponse.title: TagResponse
TagResponse.description: One issued tag, in both stored and printable form.

Tier.title: Tier
Tier.description: Where a copy of the bytes can be read from.

TierResponse.title: TierResponse
TierResponse.description: One place these bytes can be fetched from.

TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
TokenResponse.description: Login and refresh response. The refresh token rides in the cookie.

TreeNodeResponse.title: TreeNodeResponse
TreeNodeResponse.description: One node of an ancestry chain or subtree.

TreeStepView.title: TreeStepView
TreeStepView.description:
One step of the lineage, without naming the item it refers to.

Depth and quantity are what a reader needs -- "this two-metre piece was cut
from a twelve-metre bolt". The ancestor's id and its own tag code are left
out: they identify other objects, which are not this reader's business.

TrustLevel.title: TrustLevel
TrustLevel.description:
How much independent corroboration a record has attracted.

Deliberately a description of the evidence, not a judgement about the
object. None of these values says anything is real, and none of them ever
should -- see the module docstring.

TrustResponse.title: TrustResponse
TrustResponse.description:
What corroboration a record has attracted. Not a verdict about the object.

``level`` describes the evidence, and the fields beneath it are that
evidence, so a reader who wants to weigh it themselves can. A payload that
carried only the level would be asking to be trusted; this one shows its
working.

TrustView.title: TrustView
TrustView.description: Who vouched, in what capacity, and how many times. Not a score.

UpdateCategoryRequest.title: UpdateCategoryRequest
UpdateCategoryRequest.description:
Mutable category metadata.

``slug`` and ``attribute_schema`` are absent, not optional. A slug is
referenced by URLs and printed tags; a schema change is a new version by
definition. Neither is reachable through this model, so neither can be
changed by any shape of request body.

UpdateProfileRequest.title: UpdateProfileRequest
UpdateProfileRequest.description:
The only two fields a user may change about themselves.

``extra="ignore"`` plus the absence of role/status/email means a request
carrying them is accepted and those fields are silently dropped -- there is
no branch that could apply them. Escalation via PATCH is structurally
impossible rather than defended against.

UserResponse.title: UserResponse
UserResponse.description: Public shape of a user. No password hash, no identity salt, ever.

UserRole.title: UserRole
UserRole.description: Who someone is in the supply chain. One role per user.

VerificationResult.title: VerificationResult
VerificationResult.description: The outcome of recomputing the hash and comparing it to the chain.
